subject.title: fix: harden security and release integrity

question: Should ClickClack unconditionally reject every private-network callback destination for existing installations, or preserve an explicit operator-approved path for trusted LAN, loopback, and VPN callbacks?
rationale: This is a genuine SSRF-boundary versus self-hosting-compatibility decision; source review can identify the break, but repository owners must define the permanent trust and upgrade contract.

options.title: Secure default with explicit allowlist
options.body: Reject private destinations by default while adding a narrow operator-configured CIDR or hostname allowlist, migration guidance, and coverage for both modes.

options.title: Public-only callbacks
options.body: Keep unconditional rejection but provide prominent upgrade documentation, diagnostics, and exact proof that existing private callbacks fail clearly rather than silently.

options.title: Split callback policy
options.body: Separate the callback-network change from the remaining hardening work until maintainers agree on the self-hosting contract.

recommendation.title: Secure default with explicit allowlist
recommendation.body: Reject private destinations by default while adding a narrow operator-configured CIDR or hostname allowlist, migration guidance, and coverage for both modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice affects ClickClack's core self-hosting and release contract, making the project-direction owner the best available decision route.
